subsection: H. Directors and Officers Liability (D&O) Insurance
text: [Harbor Ins. Co. v. Continental Bank Corp. (7th Cir. 1990) 922 F2d 357, 368 (applying Ill. law)—Bank paid $17.5 million in settlement of suit against certain directors (insureds) and other agents and employees (noninsured): D&O insurer obligated to reimburse Bank only for that portion of settlement attributable to the directors' wrongful acts] c. [3:708] Joinder of uninsured claims: Where the corporation chooses to indemnify its officers and directors for noncovered liabilities, an allocation of liability must be made between the D&O insurer and the corporation. (1) [3:709] Allocation of defense costs: Most courts hold that where a suit alleges both covered and noncovered claims against insured officers and directors, the D&O insurer is obligated to pay only those defense costs “generated in defense of covered claims.” [Okada v. MGIC Indem. Corp. (9th Cir. 1986) 823 F2d 276, 282 (applying Hawaii law)] However, if the defense expenditure is “reasonably related” to the defense of a covered claim, it can be allocated solely to the covered claim, even if it also aids in the defense of noncovered claims.
